newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SEEN UP ON BANK PAYMENTS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SEEN UP ON BANK PAYMENTS.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were likely to rise this week on the back of statutory reserve payments by banks, dealers said on Tuesday.
"The market is quiet at the moment but rates are likely to go up because banks are paying statutory reserves today so things are likely to tighten," one dealer said.

At the start of business on Tuesday, the rates for NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 22.5 percent and sold at 21.5 percent, up from Monday's 22 and 20 percent respectively.
Bankers' acceptances were being bought at 21.5 percent and sold at 20.15 percent compared to 21 and 20 percent.
The call rate was also indicated up at 18 percent from 15 percent with the Reserve Bank indicating a market surplus of Z$375.8 million at Tuesday's opening, up from Z$13 million quoted on Monday.
